title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 5 sets up a dictionary for free rank-2 modules over Λ = Z/4Z. This is the local algebra of the 4-torsion E[4] of an elliptic curve, i.e. level-4 structures, in the context of the moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. It follows the preceding section on F_2-planes and the cube/Aut(Cube) combinatorics.

Step by step:
(1) Put M_0 = M/2M, an F_2-plane.
(J) J = M_0^* is the 3-element set of nonzero vectors x_i, i ∈ J (here * means 'minus 0', not the dual).
(2) Multiplication by 2 induces an isomorphism M_0 ≅ 2M. This gives the exact sequence 0 → M_0 → M → M_0 → 0, so M is an extension of M_0 by itself.
(Torsors) For x ∈ M_0 the fibre M_x (four lifts of x) is a torsor under M_0, acting through 2M.
(3) For i ∈ J set M_i = M_{x_i}, and let M_J = ∏ M_i, a torsor under M_0^J.
(4)/(6) Since x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = 0, addition in M maps M_1 × M_2 × M_3 into the fibre over 0, namely 2M ≅ M_0. This map is equivariant for the sum M_0^3 → M_0. It therefore gives a canonical trivialisation of the contracted product ∧_{i∈J} M_i of the three M_0-torsors.
(7)–(8) Equivalently, let V_J(M_0) be the kernel of the sum map M_0^J → M_0. The torsor M_J then reduces canonically to a V_J(M_0)-torsor P_M: the fibre of the sum map over 0.

Purpose: the next page shows that (M_i, trivialisation) is the same datum as P_M, with M_i = P_M ∧ (M_0, pr_i). It also identifies V_J(M_0) with End(M_0) via u ↦ (u(x_i))_i. This is the kernel M_2(F_2) of GL_2(Z/4) → GL_2(F_2) = S_J. So the whole page describes the groupoid of free Z/4-modules of rank 2 as a 'gerbe of torsors under End(M_0)' over the groupoid of F_2-planes. It is a combinatorial model of BGL_2(Z/4) adapted to level-4 moduli, to be compared with the cube picture of the previous page.
errors: No mathematical error. M can indeed be rebuilt from M_0 and P_M. Sums inside one fibre are fixed by 2y = image of x_i in 2M. Sums M_i + M_j land in M_k and are fixed by the triple-sum trivialisation together with negation y ↦ y − 2y.
Notational ambiguity: J = M_0^* denotes M_0 minus {0}, not the dual space. For an F_2-plane the two can be identified, but the sum relation (4) uses the 'nonzero vectors' meaning.

ideas.what: Free Z/4-module of rank 2 viewed as an extension of M/2M by itself, with each fibre over a nonzero mod-2 vector an M_0-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/gerbe description of lifts from GL_2(F_2) to GL_2(Z/4) (kernel M_2(F_2))

ideas.what: Canonical trivialisation of the contracted product of the three torsors M_i, using x_1 + x_2 + x_3 = 0
ideas.modern_name: Contracted product of torsors / Baer-sum-type trivialisation

ideas.what: Reduction of the M_0^J-torsor ∏ M_i to a torsor P_M under V_J(M_0) = ker(sum), later identified with End(M_0)
ideas.modern_name: Reduction of structure group of a torsor; level-4 structure data on top of level 2

missed.claim: This page is the start of an intrinsic, coordinate-free combinatorial model of level-4 structures as torsors P_M under End(E[2]) over the S_3-set of nonzero 2-torsion points. Together with the previous page's cube/Aut(Cube) homogeneous spaces, it hints at a 'cube' model of the moduli of elliptic curves with full level-4 structure that Grothendieck never published. The algebra itself is elementary.
missed.quote: le torseur M_J sous M_0^J provient canoniquement d'un torseur sous V_J(M_0), que je note P_M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: At most of expository interest. It gives a canonical description of the fibres of X(4) → X(2) and of GL_2(Z/4)-combinatorics. Such descriptions exist in the literature in other forms.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine, correct torsor bookkeeping for Z/4-modules of rank 2. It is characteristic of Grothendieck's intrinsic style, but contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The 'can' label above the arrow M → M_0 in (2) and the diagram below it (M —can→ M_0, M —2→ M_0) indicate the two maps, reduction and multiplication by 2. Both are correctly read.
In (3) the struck-out text reads roughly 'fibre de M en x_i'. The retained text is 'x_i ∈ M_0, M_0-torseur'.
The equation after (4) is labelled (6) in the manuscript; there is no (5).
'M_0 ≃ V_{M_x}' means M_0 is identified with the translation group V of the torsor M_x.
